newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's GFM to pay a third of railway concession.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's GFM to pay a third of railway concession.

text.p: Mexican railroad operator Grupo Ferroviario Mexicano (GFM) plans to pay a third of its railroad concession, or 1.275 billion pesos, on Monday, the head of the company said on Thursday.
The payment is to the government for a 50-year concession to run the mammoth Pacifico-Norte railway and the attached Ojinaga-Topolobampo line.
"We will pay on Monday 1.275 billion pesos, which is 30 percent of the total amount of 3.940 billion pesos," GFM director general Javier Garcia told reporters.
GFM is composed of Mexican builder Empresas ICA, miner Grupo Mexico and U.S. Union Pacific. The consortium won the privatization in late June.
GFM has until the end of the year to pay the remaining portion of its bid. Garcia said the company may make its final payment and take over the railway ahead of schedule.
The Pacific-North railroad carries about 40 percent of Mexico's railway cargo traffic. Garcia said GFM aims to boost cargo by 25 percent in 1998.
The company has said it estimates investment in the railway of $425 million in the coming five years.
